flags.message: The supplied 19-page petition text ends at its signed conclusion and does not contain the Federal Circuit and Board opinions referenced as appendices, although the manifest correctly describes the fetched text as nonempty and untruncated. The prediction relies on the petition's attributed descriptions, including its acknowledgment of forfeiture, without independently verifying those opinions. No case outcome was retrieved or encountered.

The 46-page petition is marked empty_text=true and ocr_derived=false; petition.txt contains only whitespace and no questions-presented text was provisioned. The exact petition PDF web lookup yielded no readable content, and a date-bounded MCP search for the lower-court opinion returned no results. The prediction therefore rests on procedural inputs and base rates, not the legal question. Stakes are explicitly null rather than inferred from the caption; readable petition text or OCR would materially improve this cell.

The frozen distribution_count=1 appears to count the September 9 distribution for the September 28 conference on linked sealing motion 26M22, granted October 5, before this petition was docketed October 7. The distribution-stage cell has null cutoff/cut_kind. This may be a motion distribution misattributed to the cert moment; it is not a known cert outcome. I retain the supplied baseline band/count and predict a high count increment because the next entry may be the first substantive cert distribution, not a true relist. Please review event-moment attribution.

The provisioned petition (46 pages) was fetched with empty_text: true, so no text could be extracted and no questions-presented.txt exists. The forecast rests on the docket snapshot and the district-court docket retrieved through CourtListener, not on the petition's own questions.

context.json freezes distribution_count: 1, but the only distribution on the docket (Sep 9, 2026, for the Sep 28 conference) carried the linked motion 26M22 to file a supplemental appendix under seal; the petition itself was docketed Oct 7 after that motion was granted, and has not yet been distributed. The relist-increment claim here therefore measures the petition's first distribution, not a relist in the statpack's sense, and the cell was opened at a moment that predates the petition's first conference.

The sole frozen distribution (September 2 for the September 28 conference) appears to concern sealing motion 26M17, granted October 5, before October 7 petition docketing; the petition response is due November 6. Retained the supplied count=1 and baseline band, but did not interpret this as cert consideration. P(further distribution)=0.96 largely forecasts ordinary first distribution of the petition from this frozen count. Please review distribution/moment attribution to collateral motions. The sealing-motion grant was not treated as the petition outcome.

The 47-page petition is marked empty_text=true and its provisioned text is unusable; no QP or BIO text was provisioned. Opening the exact petition PDF through the web tool returned no readable content. Forecast completed from the snapshot, committed base rates, and the pre-petition September 30, 2025 D.C. Circuit opinion retrieved through MCP; exact petition framing and opposition arguments remain unassessed.

context.json freezes distribution_count=1, but the only DISTRIBUTED entry on this docket (Sep 2, 2026, Conference of 9/28/2026) is the distribution of motion 26M17 (leave to file the petition under seal with redacted copies), granted Oct 5. The petition itself was docketed Oct 7 with a response due Nov 6 and has not been distributed. The `moment: distribution` event therefore opened on a motion's distribution rather than the petition's, and the relist-increment claim is anchored on a count the petition has not actually reached. I forecast from the frozen count as instructed; a maintainer may want the distribution parser to ignore distributions of linked motions.

petition.txt is empty_text: true (47-page scan, no text layer), so no questions-presented.txt was derived. The public copy on supremecourt.gov is image-only, as are the redacted stay application and reply in No. 25A1448. My reading of the questions presented comes from the respondent's July 1, 2026 stay opposition (text-extractable) and the D.C. Circuit opinion, not from the petition; the brief in opposition, when filed, is likely to be text-extractable.

Forward-signal disclosure: the Court denied Herridge's stay application (No. 25A1448) on July 2, 2026 with Justice Kavanaugh noting he would grant. This is public information that predates the snapshot and bears directly on grant likelihood; it was decisive in holding the number near the band anchor rather than well above it. No material about this petition's own disposition was encountered; none exists.

Forward signal predating the snapshot shaped this forecast: PhRMA's time to petition from the Fifth Circuit's published Louisiana 340B decision (AbbVie v. Murrill) was extended to 2026-11-03 (application 26A356), and the Fourth Circuit granted rehearing en banc in PhRMA v. McCuskey on 2026-05-28. The grant probability here is mostly the chance this petition rides a grant or hold of the Louisiana companion; it is not this case's disposition and nothing retrieved revealed one.

The docket shows 'Response Requested' on 2026-10-06 after both respondents waived, but the frozen context carries band 'baseline' under sal-v4 (relists, CVSG, circuit only) and response_requested is null (an interim-docket field). The call for a response is the dominant grant signal on this docket and the band does not encode it, so this cell's number sits well above the baseline reached-rate anchor it is scored against by design, not by error. A cert-stage call-for-response cut in the statpack, or a band feature for it, would make the anchor comparable.

The provisioned petition manifest reports truncated=true for a 219-page filing. The questions presented, substantive petition, and relevant district-court opinion excerpts are available, so the forecast is completed, but it does not assume access to the full appendix. No BIO is provisioned; the snapshot places the requested response deadline on November 4, 2026, after this prediction.

Decisive forward signal from outside the provisioned record: the companion petition Hall v. Fleming (No. 26-193, same respondent, same Locke v. Davey question) has its brief in opposition due 2026-10-14 after an extension and thirteen amicus briefs, and the Fourth Circuit appeal underlying this cert-before-judgment petition (No. 26-1437) remains undecided with argument tentatively set for December 2026. Both predate the snapshot and shaped the forecast; neither reveals this petition's disposition.

The statpack publishes no cut for a Court-requested response after a respondent waiver, which is the strongest docket signal on this record (Oct 5, 2026 entry). The adjustment from the 5.0% baseline band anchor rests on judgment rather than a committed rate; a response-requested cut on the paid scored segment would make this class of cell anchorable.

The manifest marks the 134-page petition document truncated; supplied text ends mid-sentence at appendix App. 66. The substantive petition and appellate majority/dissent are available and informed the forecast, but the remaining district-court appendix was not available. No BIO is provisioned, consistent with the respondent's recorded waiver. This limitation did not block prediction.

The snapshot's single distribution (for the 10/16/2026 conference) was superseded by the Oct. 5, 2026 call for a response (due Nov. 4, 2026): the petition will not be considered at that conference and will be redistributed once the response and reply are in. The frozen distribution_count of 1 is therefore a conference the petition never reaches, and the relist-increment claim (0.96) is stated from that state; the near-certain redistribution is a mechanical consequence of the response request, not a relist signal. The salience band stayed at baseline despite the response request, so the evaluator's yardstick (baseline reached rate, ~5.0% pooled OT2017-OT2025) does not price that signal; the forecast does.

Forward signal from public dockets predating the snapshot, used in the forecast: the Court has already declined this exact question at least four times since Kingsley (Cope v. Cogdill, No. 21-783; Jordan v. Howell, No. 23-210, response requested, then held and dismissed under Rule 46; Lewis County v. Helphenstine, No. 23-259, response requested, three amici, denied Jan. 22, 2024; Hartman v. Short, No. 23-1097, denied June 10, 2024 at its first conference). No disposition of this petition exists; the live supremecourt.gov docket for 26-187 read on Oct. 8, 2026 matches the provisioned snapshot entry for entry.

Material advocacy/source distinction: the petition invokes Judge VanDyke's rehearing statement in support of review, but its own Appendix F at 61a and 67a–70a expressly agrees with the panel's mootness result and explains that a new abortion statute would not be restrained by the old injunction. Forecast follows the appended statement, not an inference that it dissented from the disposition. Appendix B also records Rule 60 burden/forfeiture issues. This is not a provisioning failure or outcome leakage; reasoning.md details the distinction.

The petitioners' reply brief (docketed Sep 30 2026, before the 2026-10-08 snapshot) was not among the provisioned documents under record/documents/ (petition, BIO, QP only). In forward mode I fetched it from supremecourt.gov myself and used it; other predictors in this fan-out that did not will have reasoned from a thinner common baseline. Consider adding the cert-stage reply to the document pipeline where one is on the docket before the snapshot.

Forward cell; two public signals predating the snapshot were decisive and were retrieved rather than provisioned: (1) the Solicitor General's CVSG brief on this docket (filed Sep 15 2026) recommends that the petition be granted and the judgment reversed; (2) GEO's companion petition against Washington, No. 26-71 (GEO Group v. Ferguson), was rescheduled and redistributed on Oct 6-7 2026 for the same Nov 6 2026 conference as this petition, which reads as the Court pairing the two. Neither reveals this petition's disposition. Respondents' Sep 29 supplemental briefs (also retrieved) raise two post-petition developments: Hencely v. Fluor Corp. (decided Apr 22 2026) and ICE's June 2026 revised detention standards.

Provisioned documents: petition.txt and brief-in-opposition.txt are both marked truncated in documents.json (the BIO file concatenates the State's and the class respondents' briefs; the class brief's reasons section is cut off mid-argument). The SG's amicus brief and both supplemental briefs, all on the docket before the snapshot date, were not provisioned; on a post-CVSG cell the SG brief is the single most informative filing.

gemini-baseline, codex-baseline, and claude-baseline all report a blank 44-page application extraction at prediction time. The evaluator's current document manifest marks it empty_text=false and ocr_derived=true, and the current application.txt is 50,786 bytes. The candidate-time document version is not staged, so the current OCR availability cannot verify what each candidate could read. Evaluations honor the disclosed earlier text gap and do not penalize it or use the current body to reconstruct the candidates' evidence. This is an input-provenance limitation, not evidence of leakage or an evaluation blocker.

All three candidates report that at their 2026-10-03 run the provisioned application (44 pages, fetched 2026-10-03) carried empty_text: true and a blank application.txt, so every prediction was made from the docket line and caption alone. The record staged for this evaluation now carries an OCR-derived body (documents.json: empty_text false, ocr_derived true) showing a Texas child-custody conservatorship modification and writ of attachment, with the appeal dismissed below for nonpayment of a $205 fee. Not a defect in any candidate; recorded so the OCR fallback's timing relative to the predict fan-out is visible to maintainers, since one candidate's subject-matter inference (landlord-tenant or civil-rights) was wrong for want of the text.

Salience version mismatch: the predictions froze a band under `sal-v3`, but the committed statpack.md provides `sal-v4` bands. Per the rules, segment_base_rate and brier_skill_score have been omitted.

gemini-baseline, claude-baseline, and codex-baseline freeze band baseline under sal-v3 for Term 2026, but the committed metrics/statpack.md segment table is headed sal-v4. Per the evaluation contract, segment_base_rate and brier_skill_score are omitted and base_rate_basis is null for all three. A frozen band cannot use the terminal fallback. Outcome correctness and Brier scores are unaffected; individual evaluation.md files explain the unavailable baseline.

Salience-version mismatch on every candidate (gemini-baseline, claude-baseline, codex-baseline): each prediction froze band 'baseline' under salience_version 'sal-v3', while the committed metrics/statpack.md renders the 'Segment base rate by salience band' table under 'sal-v4'. Per the evaluate prompt the table is no baseline for that band, so segment_base_rate and brier_skill_score are omitted and base_rate_basis is null on all three evaluation.json files. Note for the stamp: statpack.json still carries a sal-v3 alt_segments block (OT2017-OT2025; baseline-band reached figures pool to ~5.0% over n~12,720), so the harness's version-pinned pooling may resolve a claim baseline even though the rendered table cannot. The evaluator-written trio is left null as the prompt's only sanctioned answer.

codex-baseline's retrieval.md discloses three CourtListener MCP searches that failed with HTTP 429, but its captured retrieval_log.json (29 calls, coverage 1.0) carries no mcp call class; the only non-shell rows are two 'other' entries whose text the harness redacted as credential-shaped. The disclosed calls are therefore unobserved in the log. Not a leakage concern (forward cell, searches named companion cases only); noted because the staged log and the candidate's own disclosure cannot be reconciled from the blinded view.

Forward-cell timing relative to the conference order lists: all three candidates ran on 2026-10-04, after the 2026-10-01 grant list from the 2026-09-28 conference had issued and one day before the 2026-10-05 denial. A petition absent from the grant list is, at that point, almost certainly a denial or a relist, so a forward cell placed in that window carries a strong legitimate signal about its own disposition that the band baseline does not condition on. claude-baseline disclosed seeing other 2026-10-01 grants in a corpus query and did not look for this case; none of the three used the signal. Not leakage under the mode rules, but worth weighing in how forward distribution-moment cells are scheduled against the Court's order-list calendar.

The blinded prediction.json stages big_case_score and big_case_rationale alongside the fields the evaluator must read first, so the instruction to form the big_case read before seeing the predictor's cannot be honoured structurally. My read (0.42) was formed from the record and outcome and I did not use the predictors' values, but the independence is procedural rather than enforced.
